The result is surprising. Edit C(2.0) moved the onset logprob the wrong way: +0.095, with P(onset) rising from 0.73 to 0.78. Same-first-token novel lines are unchanged (-0.003) and references lose 0.053 nats per token. Reversing the direction made repetition slightly more likely, not less. So the correlation hides a different causal role. A plausible reading is that the onset representation partly signals "this content was already said". The network then uses that signal to resist repeating, and removing it weakens the resistance.

The dose-response test that follows is the opposite sign: amplify the direction instead (β = -1.5, W ← W + 1.5·v vᵀW in layers 16 to 22). If the onset logprob now falls with near-zero change on same-token novel lines and modest reference damage, the direction is a causal anti-repetition lever worth a generation test. If the onset logprob also rises or stays flat, the direction isn't usefully causal and I'll close the onset-direction line.

C(-1.5) is saved. It amplifies the token-matched onset direction in the outputs of layers 16 to 22 (14 tensors). This teacher-forced screen on the same 750 texts tests the opposite-sign dose. If the direction is a causal anti-repetition signal, the onset logprob should now fall, with little change on same-token novel lines and references.

Pass 12 for C(-1.5) is done, and the per-text means again changed only slightly. I'll compute the same table. If the onset logprob falls, and clearly more than the same-token novel-line control, this direction is a causal anti-repetition lever with the opposite sign to my original guess. If it doesn't, the onset-direction approach is closed.

This time the edit moves the decision in the predicted direction, and the dose response is consistent: β = +2 raised P(onset), and β = -1.5 lowers it.

|---|---|

So amplifying this "already said this" signal discourages starting and continuing repeats while leaving the reasoning text essentially untouched. That is the profile I wanted.

The real test is accuracy. I'll run a paired "both" generation on dev_b2, the last 256 DEV problems. They were not used to build the direction, since the onset texts came from dev_a and dev_b1. Two outcomes would confirm the mechanism: a clearly lower cut rate with accuracy at least as good (gain of about +2 or more), or many wrong→right flips among formerly cut answers. Unchanged cuts would refute it, as would cuts turning into wrong answers with a net loss.
